players.product: Sqale neutral-atom quantum computer (plus quantum clocks and RF sensors)

quarterly_data.signal: Infleqtion press release (8-K): Infleqtion announced a demonstration of 30 entangled logical qubits using just 80 physical qubits on its Sqale quantum computing platform, which it calls a key 2026 roadmap milestone and says makes it the first neutral-atom quantum computing company to reach 30 logical qubits on a commercial system; the result was confirmed by a signal approximately 1000x stronger than underlying noise, the experiment executed approximately 1,000 physical operations, and it used a new logical entangling operation found with AI assistance (GPT 5.6 Sol) that needs 4 instead of 8 physical two-qubit gates. CEO Matt Kinsella: 'We're moving quickly toward our target of 100 logical qubits in 2028'; the company says it remains on track to deliver 100 logical qubits in 2028 and 1,000 by 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: 30 logical qubits with 80 physical qubits; 100 logical qubits in 2028; 1,000 by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Wellcome Leap: Infleqtion press release (8-K) - Infleqtion has three customers for logical qubit circuits on the Sqale platform, among them the Wellcome Leap Quantum for Bio (Q4Bio) program, where it demonstrated on hardware a quantum neural network approach with training on GPU and inference on QPU for biomarker discovery, first at 12 logical qubits.
quarterly_data.figure: three customers for logical qubit circuits

quarterly_data.signal: Infleqtion Quantum World Congress presentation (8-K, CEO Matt Kinsella): ~$45M FY26 revenue guidance; 248+ patents issued and pending; 175+ physicists and engineers; systems deployed in the U.S., U.K., Japan and Australia; hundreds of quantum customers across government, enterprise and research; a 50+ logical qubit system planned; government programs include ARPA-E QC3, the Genesis Mission (3) and a $100M Department of Commerce investment.
